questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the core difference between what a budget threshold catches and what an anomaly alert catches?
options: A budget catches planned-vs-actual drift against a set amount; an anomaly alert catches a sudden, unusual spending pattern even far under any budget
A budget only works in AWS, while an anomaly alert only works in Azure
There is no real difference — both require the same manually set percentage threshold
A budget monitors usage units, while an anomaly alert only monitors dollar amounts
questions.explain: A budget is a set threshold that catches overspend relative to a plan, while an anomaly alert catches an unexpected shape in spend without needing any threshold set at all — they catch different kinds of problems.

questions.q: In the Azure Budget example in this lesson, what does an action group attached to an alert threshold let you do?
options: Automatically delete the resource that caused the overspend
Do more than notify a person — e.g. email, trigger a webhook, or call an Azure Function
Permanently lower the subscription's spending limit
Convert the budget into an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor
questions.explain: An Azure action group can route a crossed threshold to email, a webhook, an Azure Function, or a Logic App — it's not limited to sending a person a notification.

questions.q: Which AWS Budget type alerts when the percentage of usage covered by a Savings Plan or Reservation drops below a target?
options: A cost budget
A usage budget
A forecasted budget
A coverage budget
questions.explain: Savings Plans/Reservation coverage budgets specifically track the share of usage covered by a commitment discount, signaling that usage shifted or a commitment expired.

questions.q: What makes AWS Cost Anomaly Detection and Azure Cost Management anomaly detection different from a manually set budget threshold?
options: They can only be configured by AWS or Microsoft support staff, never by the account owner
They only run once per year, at the start of the fiscal year
They use machine-learning-based detection against historical spend patterns, with no manually set threshold required
They require every resource to already have a Savings Plan or Reservation applied
questions.explain: Both tools learn what's normal from the scope's own historical spend and flag deviations from that learned pattern, rather than relying on a threshold someone had to pick manually.

questions.q: When AWS Cost Anomaly Detection flags an anomaly, what does the alert specifically identify to speed up root-cause analysis?
options: The exact engineer who deployed the resource that caused the spike
The top contributor — the specific service or resource that drove the unexpected change
A recommendation to immediately cancel all Reserved Instances
The subscription's total forecasted spend for the next twelve months
questions.explain: The anomaly alert names the top contributor, pointing directly at the service or resource responsible — usually faster than starting from a Cost Explorer report and working backward.
